The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent PAGASA forecasts and global model guidance for Metro Manila point to a daytime high of 33–35°C on May 24, with partly cloudy skies and a 20–40% chance of afternoon showers that could limit peak heating. Trader consensus has converged on 36°C and 37°C because May’s pre-monsoon conditions feature intense solar insolation and urban heat-island effects that routinely push actual maxima 1–3°C above official guidance when cloud cover remains limited. Key variables differentiating these outcomes include the strength and timing of any easterly waves or low-pressure troughs, which control afternoon convection and evaporative cooling, versus clearer periods that allow greater boundary-layer warming. Historical May climatology shows frequent 34–36°C peaks, with occasional 37–38°C readings when the intertropical convergence zone stays suppressed, creating the tight probability spread currently observed.
